title: Roof Work & Fragile Surfaces
whatItIs: Almost one in five workers killed in construction are doing roof work. Most fall from roof edges, or through holes, roof lights and other fragile surfaces.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT work on or near a fragile surface if the job can reasonably be done safely without it.
If you must, platforms, coverings or guard rails MUST be used to take your weight.
Prominent warning notices MUST be fixed at the approach to a fragile surface.
Materials MUST NOT be thrown or tipped from height where they could injure anyone.

keyFacts: Don't trust any sheeted roof and don't stand on it. Never walk along the bolt lines or the ridge.
Roof lights can be hard to see or painted over: cover them, or put barriers round them.

visual.caption: Likely to be fragile (INDG401). Approach a fragile roof as if the sheets weren't there

items.title: Roof lights
items.text: Some are hard to see in certain light; others are hidden by paint.

items.title: Fibre cement sheets
items.text: Non-reinforced sheets. Asbestos cement gets more fragile with age.

items.title: Metal sheets and liner panels
items.text: Corroded metal sheets; liner panels on built-up sheeted roofs.

items.title: Glass, chipboard, slates, tiles
items.text: Glass (including wired glass), rotted chipboard, slates and tiles.

a.label: Sloping roof
points: Roof ladder hooked over the ridge; don't walk on tiles

b.label: Flat roof
points: Short job: harness, secure anchor, short lanyard

onTheTest.question: You need to cross an old cement-sheet roof to reach a gutter. What is the safe approach?
options: Walk along the line of the roof bolts
Use staging and protection, or avoid going on it
Step only where the sheets look solid
onTheTest.why: HSG150 paras 240-242: don't trust or stand on any sheeted roof, or walk on the bolt lines or ridge. Work from below or a MEWP, or use staging with protection.

onTheTest.question: What is the most HSG150 says should be carried up a ladder onto a roof?
onTheTest.why: HSG150 para 235: the maximum load that should be carried up a ladder is 10 kg. A safe way of lifting materials to roof level must be provided.

traps: A quick job on a roof is still dangerous: even short work needs safe access and a safe way to work.
Walking on the bolt lines or the ridge doesn't make a fragile roof safe: the sheets can still crack.
Don't throw old slates or tiles down: use an enclosed chute or lower them in containers.
A pack of roof sheets is not a safe working platform.
